history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was an initiative proposed by Harvard University to investigate the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere, primarily to enhance computer models assessing the ecological impacts of solar geoengineering. Led by Frank Keutsch and his team, the experiment was publicly discussed, notably at the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017. It aimed to study aerosol microphysics and chemistry rather than to conduct a geoengineering deployment or induce planetary cooling. The experiment involved a scientific balloon gondola operating at approximately 20 km altitude, releasing a minimal quantity of material—ranging from 100 grams to under 2 kilograms of calcium carbonate—into a defined plume. A planned hardware test in Sweden was ultimately suspended by the SCoPEx Advisory Committee due to the need for broader societal dialogue, ensuring no particles were emitted. In March 2024, it was announced that SCoPEx would not proceed as originally intended, with plans to redirect the platform towards unrelated stratospheric research. This cautious approach reflects an awareness of the potential implications for ozone, ecosystems, and unintended ecological consequences.
